metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results (Volume IV) Factsheets – United States

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 financial literacy results for the United States using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The assessment is based on a complex multi-stage sampling design of schools and students, and OECD reporting typically relies on PISA sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates; however, the factsheet itself does not specify the exact weight variable names or replicate-weight method. The financial literacy domain is assessed with a computer-based test and is administered in a split design where students take either financial literacy plus mathematics/reading, while both groups receive a total of 120 minutes across the two parts. Plausible values are used for cognitive achievement reporting in PISA, but this factsheet does not document the PV combination or missing-data procedures; readers are directed to the Reader’s Guide and Volume IV annexes for technical details.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing descriptive PISA 2022 financial literacy results (means and proficiency-level distributions) rather than an empirical modeling study that specifies how plausible values and missing data were processed. Plausible values handling is therefore not applicable for the extraction target here because no PV estimation/combination method is described in the provided text. Missing-data handling is not reported in the factsheet excerpt because the technical procedures are deferred to the PISA Reader’s Guide and Volume IV annexes.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the analytic population for the United States that participated in the PISA 2022 financial literacy assessment. It does not describe additional exclusions (e.g., missing questionnaire items, incomplete test participation) in the provided excerpt; therefore, the filtering criteria are not specified beyond being part of the financial literacy assessment sample.

This indicates that mean score was 505 (not significantly different from the OECD average of 498), with 17% below Level 2 and 13.5% at Level 5, and it also provides comparisons to prior PISA financial literacy cycles.

data.outcome_summary: PISA 2022 financial literacy was administered as the fourth cycle of this domain, with the United States participating in 2012, 2015, 2018, and again in 2022. Financial literacy was assessed via a computer-based test, with students in sampled schools split into two groups: one group took financial literacy plus either mathematics or reading, while the other group took the core PISA subjects (mathematics, reading, science); both groups received a total of 120 minutes. The assessment used a mix of multiple-choice and constructed-response items organized around real-life passages, and students completed a background questionnaire covering attitudes, home experiences, and learning about financial matters. In the United States, 3 206 students participated in the financial literacy assessment (representing over 3.5 million 15-year-olds). The factsheet reports that the U.S. mean score was 505 (not significantly different from the OECD average of 498), with 17% below Level 2 and 13.5% at Level 5, and it also provides comparisons to prior PISA financial literacy cycles.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an OECD PISA 2022 country factsheet, which is primarily descriptive and does not present an original student-level predictive/ML modeling pipeline. As a result, fields related to ML techniques, PV combination methods, and missing-data handling are not specified in the provided text and are instead referenced to the PISA Reader’s Guide and Volume IV annexes. The factsheet reports proficiency distributions and mean comparisons rather than model-based effects with documented estimation procedures.
